draft_key_information_units.information: Annual headline financial performance metrics for 2025 including like-for-like rental income growth of 4.9% (5.6% in 2024), real economic occupancy of 98.5% (flat year-on-year), annual net operating income margin of 72.1% (70.3% in 2024), property values up 2.9% (2.6%) year-on-year driven by NOI growth and value-accretive capex, privatization sales of SEK 10,664 million (2,466 residential units sold at a 28.9% premium to book value), SEK 44,900 million of asset-backed financing and SEK 14,600 million of capital markets issuance (six green transactions), and improved credit metrics with net loan-to-value (Net LTV) at 52.2% (56.4%) and interest coverage ratio (ICR) at 2.0x (1.9x).
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: MD&A: 2025 in Brief, Key Figures table, Funding section

draft_key_information_units.information: Q4 2025 performance highlights showing like-for-like rental growth of 4.6% (5.3% in Q4 2024), rental income of SEK 3,945 million (down 3.4% year-on-year), real economic occupancy of 98.7% (98.6% in Q4 2024), net operating income margin of 70.2% (70.2% in Q4 2024) with LTM margin of 72.1% (70.3% in 2024), privatization sales of SEK 2,890 million (798 units sold at a 32.5% premium vs 24% in Q4 2024), property values up 0.5% (0.7% in Q4 2024), a goodwill impairment loss of SEK 3,707 million, and credit metrics with Net LTV at 52.2% (56.4%) and ICR at 2.0x (1.9x).
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: MD&A: Q4 Highlights, Key Figures table for Q4

draft_key_information_units.information: Key operational performance drivers including standing assets contributing SEK 800 million rental income growth through indexation, tenant improvements, and occupancy improvements; like-for-like rental growth decomposed into indexations (3.3% of 4.9% annual growth), tenant improvements (0.7%), occupancy improvements (0.7%), and rent reversion (0.2%); property expenses decreasing 6.1% annually to SEK 4,378 million (cost control and digitalisation); and capital expenditures of SEK 3,893 million allocated across maintenance (SEK 1,790m), sustainability (SEK 557m), tenant improvements (SEK 1,168m), and value-add (SEK 241m) categories.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: MD&A: Rental Income Development, Like-for-like Development, Property Expenses, Asset Management sections

draft_key_information_units.information: Country-specific investment property fair value developments: Sweden fair values up SEK 717 million (0.8% growth) driven by strong rental performance; Germany up SEK 926 million (1.2%) despite shifted privatisation strategy; Denmark up SEK 4,643 million (7.2%) from ownership market performance; Czechia up SEK 1,856 million (6.7%) from rental performance; Netherlands up SEK 1,424 million (5.4%) from privatisation as highest and best use; Norway down SEK 382 million (-2.7%) from increased buy-to-let supply; United Kingdom down SEK 20 million (-0.4%) from stabilising yields; Poland up SEK 173 million (4.1%) from rental growth; Finland up SEK 161 million (4.3%) from rent reversion via tenant improvements.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: MD&A: Investment Properties, Country Fair Value Development section

draft_key_information_units.information: Liquidity, cash-flow, financing, and capital developments including Heimstaden Bostad completing SEK 59,500 million financing (refinancings and new financings) across unsecured capital markets and bank financing; liability management exercises in January 2025 issuing SEK 750 million senior unsecured floating rate notes and EUR 430 million/400 million fixed rate notes while tendering existing maturities; interest expenses of SEK 6,536 million (average rate 3.43% vs 3.01% in 2024); interest coverage ratio improving to 2.0x (1.9x); net loan-to-value decreasing to 52.2% (56.4%); and unutilised credit facilities of SEK 23,449 million at parent level.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: MD&A: Funding section, Interest Expenses, Liability Management, Alternative Performance Measures

draft_key_information_units.information: Material post-reporting-period events: In December 2025, an arbitration award favouring Heimstaden was received in the Alecta-initiated case, confirming no breach of the Shareholders' Agreement of Heimstaden Bostad; subsequently, in January 2025, Heimstaden Bostad issued a EUR 500 million perpetual hybrid maturity to replace the EUR 500 million perpetual hybrid resetting in April 2026.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: MD&A: Q4 Highlights (arbitration), Funding section (hybrid bond)

draft_key_information_units.information: Sustainability performance including weather-corrected energy intensity reduced by 10% (exceeding the 2% target) to 148 kWh/m²; GHG emissions reduced by 14.2% against the 2020 baseline (on track for 42% reduction by 2030); EU Taxonomy-aligned revenue at 22% (26% in 2024) and capex at 18% (22% in 2024); and green assets valued at approximately SEK 76 billion supporting green bond issuance of SEK 13,767 million in FY25, with sustainability-linked loans of SEK 5,818 million all meeting KPIs.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Sustainability Report: Highlights, E1 sections, EU Taxonomy tables

evaluation.selection_rationale: These units cover material summary-level content required for a concise financial-report summary: headline annual and quarterly performance (D1, D2), key operational drivers and cost management (D3), portfolio valuation dynamics by country (D4), liquidity/capital structure and financing developments (D5), significant post-reporting events impacting legal and funding position (D6), and sustainability performance integral to strategy and risk profile (D7). Each unit represents an independently omittable theme supported exclusively by the SOURCE FINANCIAL REPORT, with no routine boilerplate included. The selection aligns with prioritization guidelines focusing on financial performance, period-over-period changes, drivers, segment developments, liquidity, strategic events, and material sustainability metrics.
